title: Converge Core, Advanced, and Full tool surfaces without capability loss
summary: Result Goal 3 of ISS-20260730-AE1BCC for the next reliability release line. The RC6 gate was satisfied at exact released revision 2a48486b7b8c3395d05e4f30201e968ee88f9779. T1 is ready to establish one authoritative stable/compatibility/experimental/retired tool inventory and freeze Core/Advanced/Full exposure invariants without changing permissions or removing callable capabilities. Final rh_work and E2E stages depend on the evidence and context foundations.
goals: Create one authoritative tool inventory and exposure classification for Core, Advanced, and Full.
Shrink Core to a small model-friendly facade without deleting or permission-gating underlying capabilities.
Guarantee all stable typed tools remain callable through Advanced/Full and that Core omissions return explicit capability/routing guidance.
Run a dual-connector Shadow period and switch defaults only after measured correctness, latency, payload, and fallback gates pass.
nonGoals: Do not use tool exposure profiles as a replacement for authorization or repository access policy.
Do not remove stable typed tools merely to reduce Core schema size.
Do not force specialist iOS, Browser, ASC, Git, Campaign, Agent, Recovery, or runtime workflows through an impoverished generic facade.
Do not switch the default Connector before Shadow criteria are met.
Do not duplicate tool registries in CLI, Gateway, tests, and documentation.
acceptanceCriteria: A single authoritative inventory generates or validates profile membership, schemas, documentation, snapshots, and fingerprints.
Core remains intentionally small; Advanced contains every stable typed capability; Full is a superset for compatibility and maintenance.
Core hidden tools are distinguishable from permission denied and return unsupported_in_core with required capability, reason, and Advanced route where applicable.
Category-level invocation E2E proves Advanced/Full tools are actually callable, not merely present in tools/list.
Core facade E2E proves ordinary repository work remains correct and specialist tasks route without capability loss.
Core, Advanced, and Full expose distinct stable fingerprints and satisfy Full >= Advanced > Core.
Dual Connector Shadow collects correctness, tool-selection, fallback, payload, latency, and unsupported-route metrics before any default switch.
Existing authorization, strong confirmation, resource claims, secret handling, and remote-write gates behave identically across profiles.
relatedArtifacts: ISS-20260730-A1EA53 (required before final Core work/finalize schema)

tasks.title: Establish the authoritative tool inventory and exposure invariants
tasks.objective: After RC6 is clean, inventory all registered stable, compatibility, experimental, and retired tools; identify every duplicated membership source; define generation/validation rules, profile fingerprints, and capability categories without changing runtime exposure yet.
acceptanceCriteria: RC6 terminal merged revision is recorded.
Every currently callable stable tool has one canonical identity and capability category.
Core/Advanced/Full invariants and permission-independence are represented as machine tests.
Retired tools are explicitly classified rather than silently disappearing.
notes: Controller-enforced external gate. Unblock to ready only after ISS-20260729-BF2F89 is terminal, integrated, cleaned, and its exact revision has been recorded. Tool-surface work remains an exposure/schema optimization and must not alter permissions or stable capability availability.

RC6 external gate is satisfied at exact released revision 2a48486b7b8c3395d05e4f30201e968ee88f9779; current origin/main is 809349d43b6583b4cfa22e55986f760f16380cb3. Start with read-only authoritative inventory and invariant freezing only. Tool exposure profiles remain architecture/schema choices, never permission tiers; all stable Advanced/Full capability categories must remain callable and later receive category-level invocation E2E.

tasks.title: Implement the bounded Core exposure profile
tasks.objective: Create the minimal Core profile around rh_access, rh_status, rh_inbox, rh_context, rh_work, session binding, bounded search/read, and safe patching while preserving Advanced and Full registries.
acceptanceCriteria: Core target is 5–7 facade tools and does not exceed 10 without a documented gate exception.
Advanced still exposes all stable typed tools and Full preserves compatibility/maintenance tools.
Profile selection does not alter authorization decisions or underlying action policy.
Profile fingerprints and tools/list snapshots are deterministic.

tasks.title: Add explicit Core-to-Advanced capability routing
tasks.objective: For capabilities intentionally absent from Core, return structured unsupported_in_core guidance with required capability, why specialist routing is needed, and the Advanced entry point; ensure specialist prompts can select Advanced directly.
acceptanceCriteria: Unsupported Core actions never masquerade as permission denial or missing installation.
Every stable Advanced capability category has a tested discovery/routing path from Core context.
No generic facade bypasses strong typed schemas for high-risk specialist actions.
Fallback is bounded and observable.

tasks.title: Converge the Core rh_work schema on evidence and context contracts
tasks.objective: After the execution-evidence baseline and action ContextRequirements are stable, simplify rh_work inputs/outputs while preserving objective, acceptance, path, check, evidence, approval, recovery, and context-resolution references needed for safe continuation.
acceptanceCriteria: Core schema size drops materially without hiding state required for trustworthy completion.
A new session can continue from Core output using stable Work and context references.
Specialist fields remain in typed Advanced actions instead of being flattened into rh_work.
Compatibility callers receive deterministic migration behavior.

tasks.title: Prove Core ordinary flows and Advanced category callability
tasks.objective: Build E2E suites for Core session/context/search/read/patch/work/verify/finalize flows and category-level Advanced/Full invocation for repository, Git, Agent, Campaign/legacy migration, Recovery, runtime, iOS, Browser, ASC, and plugin actions.
acceptanceCriteria: Tests invoke representative tools in every stable capability category.
All tools required for final Apple and reliability work remain callable.
Core facade flows complete with evidence and cleanup rather than tools/list-only assertions.
Permission and authorization results match across exposure profiles.

tasks.title: Run dual-connector Shadow with measurable fallback
tasks.objective: Operate Core and Advanced connectors side by side, keep Advanced as the default, collect schema payload, latency, tool-selection correctness, unsupported routes, fallback frequency, task success, and capability-loss signals, and document rollback.
acceptanceCriteria: Shadow cannot delete or disable Advanced/Full.
Metrics distinguish Core design gaps from permissions, plugin readiness, and task failures.
Fallback to Advanced is explicit, bounded, and succeeds for representative specialist tasks.
Rollback to Advanced-only requires no state migration.

tasks.title: Decide and verify the default Core cutover
tasks.objective: Use predeclared Shadow thresholds to accept, defer, or reject Core as the default model-facing connector; verify no capability loss and retain Advanced/Full escape paths.
acceptanceCriteria: Default changes only when success, fallback, latency, payload, and capability-callability gates pass.
A failed gate leaves Advanced as default without partial cutover.
Release notes and runbooks explain Core versus Advanced versus Full without describing them as permission tiers.
All implementation worktrees are merged and cleaned.
